checksums.name: duplicated_guard_byte_0x0E_0x0F_write_transaction_token
checksums.formula_detail: NOT a data checksum. FUN_0803f2c0 (decompiled.c:2075-2091): b=FUN_08043830() low byte (LCG: state=state*_DAT_08043844+1, return state>>16; constants unresolved in export); write b at SRAM 0x0E, write payload, write same b at 0x0F. Validation FUN_0803f00c (1938-1951) only checks magic and byte[0x0E]==byte[0x0F] (with an unresolved '2'/0 legacy exception). Falsified as sum/xor/CRC over payload: cap-00 payload sum8=0x03 xor8=0x01 crc32_lo=0x88 vs stored 0x88 (coincidence) but cap-01 sum8=0x06 xor8=0x00 crc32_lo=0x07 vs stored 0xB4; stored delta +0x2C while payload byte-sum delta is +3 (three 0->1 flags). See SAVE-FORMAT-REPORT.md sec.4 for full Python table.

io_driver_functions.notes: SRAM write wrapper: if len!=0 call FUN_080c3fa4(src, offset|0x0E000000, len) write-with-verify; clears *_DAT_0803fdcc first. Tail-call (UNRECOVERED_JUMPTABLE) so callgraph callees are empty; callers from textual grep of decompiled.c.
SRAM read wrapper: func_0x080c61a8(offset|0x0E000000, dst, len, *_DAT_0803fdfc). Same tail-call caveat.
Write-with-verify, up to 3 attempts: FUN_080c3e80 byte-copy to SRAM then func_0x080c61a8 compare; break on match (decompiled.c:4804-4819).
Byte-at-a-time SRAM copy *dst++=*src++; first masks/sets WAITCNT-like *_DAT_080c3eb8 with |3 (decompiled.c:4748-4763). No Flash 0x5555/0x2AAA sequence and no EEPROM DMA3 bitstream anywhere in corpus.

ROM-library SRAM read/compare thunk at 0x080C61A8; body not recovered (jumptable stub, decompiled.c:5834-5845), role inferred from both call sites. Confidence CONFIRMED_STATIC for role, UNKNOWN for internals.
Erase: fills all 0x8000 SRAM bytes with 0xFF in 8-byte FUN_0803fd90 writes (2430-2451). Proves 32768-byte media and fill byte.
Transactional writer: guard byte at 0x0E, payload at (offset,len), same guard at 0x0F. Every sub-block flush goes through it.

Guard-byte generator, LCG state=state*mult+1, return state>>16 (3927-3935). NOT a checksum over data. Multiplier/seed DAT constants not resolved in this Ghidra export, so exact byte sequence cannot be recomputed from .sav alone.

open_questions: FUN_08043830 LCG multiplier (*_DAT_08043844), state address/seed (*_DAT_08043840) and exact byte extraction (extraout_var) are unresolved DAT in this export, so the guard-byte sequence cannot be recomputed or predicted; only its equality role is proven.
Block E (8B) and F (4B) SRAM offsets are inferred (0x424/0x42C) from contiguity + FUN_08003df8 stack layout; the literal *_DAT_0803f708/*_DAT_0803f730 values were not in the export.

Block C (0x368, 32B) changed at +0x1C between samples but has no non-init writer in the 168-function trace-guided corpus; its writer and all C semantics are unknown - the corpus is a subset, not the whole ROM.

No fixed EWRAM (0x02xxxxxx) or IWRAM (0x03xxxxxx) save-struct mirror could be proven: every traced caller mutates stack copies (in_stack buffers in FUN_08003df8/FUN_080438bc/FUN_0803f074) and flushes whole blocks; the param_1 handle from FUN_0803fd20 is opaque. Any report claiming a RAM base would be guessing.

Records at 0x10+idx*8 (FUN_0803f30c), 0xC0+idx*0x1C x13 (FUN_0803f390) and 0x2000 (FUN_0803f748) have readers but no writers in the corpus and are all-0xFF in both samples; their producers, record counts (0x10 region extent) and semantics are unknown.

FUN_080436bc's 25-entry code table and FUN_080438bc's param_1 codes are unresolved DAT, so B-flag indices (including observed B+0x11) cannot be named after specific gallery items without further ROM data extraction.
FUN_0803f00c's legacy exception (cStack_a=='2' && cStack_9=='\0' bypasses E==F) is unexplained - possibly an old-version header migration - and untested on real samples (neither sample uses it).
FUN_080c61a8 (SRAM read/compare) and FUN_080c3f0c bodies are jumptable stubs; WAITCNT details in FUN_080c3e80 (*_DAT_080c3eb8 |3) could not be resolved to a named register value.

The two samples differ by only three flag bytes and both are near-factory state; high-value fields (scores, timers, multi-byte counters inside A/C/D) cannot be distinguished from padding without a more progressed save.
